verdict.one_line: Downgraded from Green: accounting is now confirmed clean (FY2024/FY2025 unqualified, CAG nil both years) but the board breached the SEBI LODR 50% independent-director requirement for parts of FY2026, was fined Rs.10.86 lakh by BSE+NSE (waiver pending, not yet granted), and a 2026 CBI recruitment-fraud probe is open at a NALCO site — together these move governance from a data-gap Green-lean to an active, disclosed, penalized compliance gap that gates the verdict at Amber pending SEBI/NCLT docket confirmation and CBI outcome.
verdict.provisional_reason: legal_regulatory sub-score remains provisional: SEBI enforcement-order and NCLT/NCLAT docket-level search was attempted twice (original DR1 + DR1-B follow-up) and both times returned only an absence-of-evidence result — the portals are interactive/form-driven and not indexable by the search/fetch tooling available. Treat as 'unverified-clean, disclosed gap' rather than confirmed clean. Also outstanding: waiver outcome on the BSE/NSE ID-composition fine, and the CBI recruitment-fraud probe status (ongoing/closed).

sub_scores.rationale: RESOLVED (prior provisional gate closed). Unqualified audit opinions confirmed for all 5 years reviewed: FY2021 [SRC-119], FY2022 [SRC-210], FY2023 [SRC-3469], FY2024 [SRC-2702, F-AUD-03], FY2025 [SRC-2752, F-AUD-24] — joint statutory auditors A.K. Sabat & Co./P.A. & Associates (FY2024) and B M Chatrath & Co. LLP/SRB & Associates (FY2025) per facts/fragments/facts_AR_FY24_25_audit.json. CAG Section 143(6) supplementary-audit comment confirmed 'Nil — Nothing significant has come to knowledge' for both FY2024 [F-AUD-04] and FY2025 [F-AUD-25] — closes the CAG-comment open question from the company's own AR disclosure (external DR1-B docket search separately could not corroborate or contradict this from the primary CAG report list — see legal_regulatory sub-score — so treat as company-disclosed-nil, not externally certified-nil). Contingent liabilities: FY2024 Rs.1,920.03cr [F-AUD-05], FY2025 Rs.2,050.43cr [F-AUD-27] — both within the FY2021-FY2023 range (Rs.2,153-2,378cr) and show no step-change or emerging litigation category; itemized breakdown (sales tax, customs, income tax, land acquisition, PSU/OHPC energy-compensation claims etc.) is granular and consistent between the two years, no new categories appearing. One item of note: FY2025 audit disclosed a payroll-software audit-trail gap (audit-trail feature not enabled) [F-AUD-26] — a control-deficiency disclosure, not a qualification, and immaterial to the opinion; kept visible here as a governance-hygiene item rather than folded silently into the clean rating. Forensic earnings-quality flags (other income 25.9% of CFO in FY2023 RF-001; DSO increases RF-002/RF-003) remain 'candidate' status, moderate not severe. No restatement evidence at any point FY2021-FY2025. Score raised from 82 (provisional) to 90 reflecting the closed gate; held below high-90s only for the payroll-audit-trail control gap and the still-open external CAG-report-PDF corroboration.

DOWNGRADED from 80. New, load-bearing finding (F-EXT-1155, confidence high, corroborated across 4 sources SRC-1160/1161/1162/1163): NALCO's own FY2026 Annual Secretarial Compliance Report admits the board fell short of SEBI LODR Regulation 17(1)'s minimum 50% independent-director requirement during parts of FY2026, following the 31-Mar-2026 tenure-expiry cessation of three independent directors (Trupti Kamlesh Patel, Ajay Narang, Patel Sanjaykumar) without named replacements — this also degraded Audit Committee, Nomination & Remuneration Committee, and Stakeholders Relationship Committee composition. BSE and NSE each fined NALCO Rs.5,42,800 (total Rs.10,85,600 incl. 18% GST) via notices dated 27-Feb-2026 for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2025. NALCO requested a waiver (17-Mar-2026 letter) citing that ID appointments are the exclusive prerogative of the President of India/Ministry of Mines, outside company control — a structurally accurate CPSE point, but the fine was levied and the waiver outcome is not yet reported, so this is scored as an active, exchange-penalized compliance breach, not a resolved routine vacancy. This is a materially worse characterization than the prior pass's 'board appointments are political, structural feature, not independently verified' framing — it reframes from a data-gap to a confirmed compliance failure. Separately, a 2026 CBI probe (F-EXT-1156, confidence medium) into recruitment-fraud allegations (~20 people allegedly promised/given jobs at NALCO's Haradghana site without official advertisement) is open; NALCO's public rebuttal frames the CBI visit as routine verification of an unverified external complaint (no raid/seizure), and it is not a confirmed adverse finding against management — held as a governance watch item, weighted lightly relative to the ID-composition breach given lower confidence and no admission of wrongdoing. RPT structure (CPSE/GoI inter-entity trade, KMP remuneration trend) is unchanged from the prior pass and remains a Green-leaning factor within this sub-score, partially offsetting the board-composition downgrade. No promoter pledge (sovereign promoter, N/A) unchanged. Net: rubric's Amber trigger for governance ('frequent auditor changes, large RPTs' as illustrative Amber examples) is better read here as 'disclosed board-composition non-compliance with a regulatory fine' as the operative Amber-to-Red-leaning driver — scored 58, Amber, not Red, because (a) the breach is company-self-disclosed and being remediated/appealed rather than concealed, (b) it is a structural CPSE appointment-control issue rather than promoter misconduct, and (c) the fine is monetary/procedural (~Rs.10.86 lakh), not a finding of fraud or diversion.

DOWNGRADED from 70. The BSE/NSE fine for LODR Reg. 17(1) non-compliance (F-EXT-1155) is itself a regulatory-enforcement action (exchange-level, not SEBI-order-level) and is now counted directly in this sub-score, not just in governance — a monetary fine for board-composition breach is a legal/regulatory fact, waiver not yet granted. The 2026 CBI recruitment-fraud probe (F-EXT-1156) is a second, lower-confidence open item: an external-complaint-triggered inquiry, not (per available evidence) a chargesheet or finding against the company. Both are held to Amber-severity per rubric ('ongoing investigations' = Amber trigger), not Red (no criminal charge or regulator order against the company/promoter has been confirmed). SEBI-enforcement-order and NCLT/NCLAT docket-level search was attempted twice (original DR1 pass + DR1-B follow-up, F-EXT-1157) and both times returned only an absence-of-evidence result — the relevant portals (sebi.gov.in/enforcement, nclt.gov.in, nclat.nic.in) are interactive/form-driven case-search tools not indexable by the search/fetch tooling used; this is explicitly flagged by DR1-B as 'unverified-clean, disclosed gap,' per the coordinator's framing, and is carried forward here rather than assumed clean. CAG Section 143(6) FY2023-FY2025 para search (F-EXT-1158) also remains unresolved externally — the company's own 'Nil' CAG comment (now confirmed via extraction, see accounting sub-score) is neither corroborated nor contradicted by an independently-fetched CAG report PDF. AOC-1/JV litigation facts still not extracted. Score of 62 (Amber) reflects: one confirmed, fined compliance breach + one open lower-confidence probe, against a backdrop of an unresolved (not negative) SEBI/NCLT/CAG docket sweep. This sub-score cannot be moved to Green or confirmed at a stable Amber level until either (a) the SEBI/NCLT docket search is upgraded to a certified query, (b) the CBI probe resolves, or (c) the BSE/NSE waiver outcome is reported.

No outright refusals found in any of the 4 transcripts. Score held at 80.
